 Fast charge your iPhone - Apple Support 
 Fast charge your iPhone
 Find out what you need to fast charge your iPhone.
 What you need
 iPhone 18 Pro models and iPhone Duo
 To fast charge iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max up to 50 percent battery in around 15 minutes, or iPhone Duo up to 50 percent battery in around 20 minutes, use the USB-C cable that came in the box, and one of these adapters:
 Apple 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max
 A comparable third-party 60W-capable (or greater) adapter that uses Adjustable Voltage Supply (AVS) and supports USB Power Delivery (USB-PD) 3.2
 iPhone 17 models and iPhone Air
 You can fast charge iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, and iPhone 17 Pro Max up to 50 percent battery in around 20 minutes with a 40W adapter or higher. For iPhone 17e and iPhone Air, use a 20W adapter or higher to charge up to 50 percent battery in around 30 minutes.
 Earlier iPhone models
 To fast charge an iPhone 15 or later, use a USB-C cable , like the one that came in the box, or use a USB-C to Lightning cable with an earlier iPhone model. You need one of these adapters:
 Apple 18W or greater USB-C Power Adapter
 A comparable third-party USB-C power adapter that supports USB-PD
 Wireless fast charging
 To wirelessly charge iPhone 18 Pro models and iPhone Duo up to 50 percent in around 30 minutes, use a MagSafe Charger and a 35W or higher adapter.
 For iPhone 16, iPhone 17, and iPhone Air use a MagSafe Charger and one of these adapters:
 Apple 30W or greater USB-C Power Adapter
 A comparable third-party USB-C power adapter that supports USB Power Delivery (USB-PD)
 For iPhone 15 and earlier, you can fast charge up to 15W with a MagSafe Charger and one of these adapters:
 Apple 20W or greater USB-C Power Adapter
 A comparable third-party USB-C power adapter that supports USB Power Delivery (USB-PD)
 Fast charging might not work in conditions that are too cold or too hot .

iPhone 17 Models Feature Faster USB-C Charging With Apple's New 'Dynamic' Power Adapter - MacRumors 
 Skip to Content 
 iPhone 17 Models Feature Faster USB-C Charging With Apple's New 'Dynamic' Power Adapter
 Tuesday September 9, 2025 3:34 pm PDT by Joe Rossignol 
 iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, and iPhone 17 Pro Max models can be charged up to 50% in around 20 minutes with a compatible USB-C power adapter, according to Apple's website.
That means iPhone 17 models offer faster USB-C charging compared to iPhone 16 models, which can be charged up to 50% in around 30 minutes with a compatible adapter.
 The ultra-thin iPhone Air has similar USB-C charging speeds as the iPhone 16 series.
 One power adapter that supports the iPhone 17's faster wired charging capabilities is Apple's new 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max . It is available to order starting today in the U.S., Canada, China, Japan, Mexico, Taiwan, and the Philippines. In the U.S., pricing is set at $39.
 As its Dynamic Power name implies, this charger can dynamically deliver up to 60W of power, despite having a smaller form factor. However, due to the thermal limitations of its compact design, the charger can only reach that 60W peak in short bursts. A larger 60W-or-higher charger does not face that limitation.
 Know that you do not need to use this specific new Apple power adapter to unlock the iPhone 17's faster charging — most higher-wattage chargers should do the trick.
 Also, remember that Apple sells USB-C charging cables separately.
 iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, and iPhone 17 Pro Max models can be pre-ordered starting this Friday at 5 a.m. Pacific Time, and the devices launch on Friday, September 19.

 Just unboxed your new iPhone 17 or thinking about an upgrade? Along with the fresh design, faster chip, and camera boost, there's one big question most people ask: Can I charge the iPhone 17 with an old charger? 
 It's a fair concern. Apple hasn't included a charger in the box for years, and if you're coming from an iPhone 14 or earlier, your Lightning cable clearly won't fit the new USB-C port on the iPhone 17. So, what's the deal?
 This guide breaks it down simply. You'll learn the basics of how the iPhone 17 charges, which old adapters and cables still work, which don't, and how to power your phone safely without slowing it down.
 Table of contents

 Can I Charge My iPhone 17 with Old Chargers?
 If you're asking, "Can I charge my new iPhone with an old charger?" the answer is usually yes. You'll just need to check three things: the connector type , the charging standard, and the charger's wattage for iPhone .
 Like the iPhone 15 and 16, the iPhone 17 now uses a USB-C port , supports the USB Power Delivery (PD) standard, and comes with a 1-meter USB-C to USB-C cable in the box. That means your old Lightning cables won't fit anymore , but many existing USB-C chargers will still work.
 Charging is also faster this year. With a 40W or higher USB-C PD adapter , you can power the iPhone 17, 17 Pro, or 17 Pro Max to about 50% in roughly 20 minutes . If your older charger doesn't hit that wattage, it'll still get the job done, just at a slower pace.
 That said, it's worth checking that your old charger and cable are in good condition . Frayed wires or loose plugs aren't safe for your new phone and can affect charging speed.
 We'll look at how different adapters and cables perform with the iPhone 17 in the next section, so you'll know exactly which ones you can keep using.
 Old Chargers and Their Compatibility with iPhone 17
 You probably have a mix of old adapters and cables lying around. Some will work just fine with your iPhone 17, while others won't fit or may charge more slowly. Here's how they stack up.
 Old USB-A adapter and Lightning cable
 Still have one of those older Apple chargers, a USB-A brick with a USB-A to Lightning cable? Maybe you were using one of those newer Lightning cables, like the Anker 641 USB-C to Lightning Cable .
 Apparently, these won't work with the iPhone 17. The new model has switched fully to USB-C , which means Lightning cables are now out of the picture .
 You can still use the USB-A adapter itself if you pick up a USB-A to USB-C cable . Charging will work, but it'll be much slower , usually capped around 10-12 watts . That's fine for overnight charging or light use, but it's far from "fast charging."
 Also, keep in mind that these older bricks lack USB Power Delivery (PD) support, the technology that allows your iPhone to negotiate higher power safely. So, while they won't harm your device, they're best seen as a backup option , not your daily go-to for quick top-ups.
 Apple or third-party 20W~30W USB-C charger
 If you've owned an iPhone 12, 13, 14, or a recent iPad, chances are you already have a USB-C adapter that supports USB Power Delivery (PD) . Maybe it's Apple's official 20W or 30W adapter, or a trusted third-party option like the Anker Nano Charger (20W) .
 These will work just fine with the iPhone 17. With the included USB-C to USB-C cable , you'll get reliable, safe charging and moderate fast speeds, around 50% in 30 minutes with the 20W model, and slightly faster with a 30W brick.
 It also works perfectly with the new ultra-thin iPhone Air , which caps charging at 20W . For many people, this setup is reliable and convenient enough for daily use, without needing to buy anything new.
 40W+ USB-C PD charger
 Already have a high-wattage USB-C charger for your MacBook, iPad Pro, or another USB-C laptop? Good news, that's the best-case scenario. With a 40W or higher USB-C PD adapter , your iPhone 17 can hit about 50% charge in just 20 minutes , the fastest wired speed currently available.
 And don't worry if your charger seems "too powerful" at 60W, 100W, or even 140W . You won't damage the battery; the iPhone only draws what it needs. Just make sure the charger supports USB Power Delivery (PD) and comes from Apple or a reputable brand like Anker for safe, consistent performance.
 Need to upgrade? Check out these best iPhone 17 chargers from Anker:
 Anker Nano charger (45W): small but mighty 
 If your old brick feels sluggish or bulky, the Anker Nano Charger (45W) is a smart little upgrade. It's a single-port USB-C charger that uses GaN technology , so it stays cool and compact without losing power. You get a full 45 watts of output , enough to fast-charge your iPhone 17 Pro Max to 50% in around 20 minutes or top up a MacBook Air fast.
 The Nano comes with a folding plug and a body that's about half the size of Apple's 30W charger , small enough to slip into a pocket or stay hidden behind a nightstand. Anker's ActiveShield safety system monitors temperature up to 6 million times a day, which helps keep both the charger and your phone in good shape.
 Anker Prime charger (160W): one charger for everything 
 If you'd rather have one brick that powers all your gear, the Anker Prime Charger (160W) fits the bill. It packs three USB-C ports and delivers a total of 160 watts , with up to 140W from a single port , enough to power a 16" MacBook Pro, while still fast-charging your iPhone 17.
 A built-in smart display shows real-time power output for each port, and the Anker app lets you check status or adjust settings over Bluetooth. You can even switch between preset AI charging modes or your own custom power setup with the touch button just below the screen.
 With PowerIQ 5.0 , it distributes power efficiently across your laptop, phone, and tablet, like using three separate chargers, but with one compact hub.
 Despite all that muscle, the Prime is surprisingly portable, roughly the size of an AirPods Pro 3 case . It's built for people who want fast, organized charging without packing a tangle of adapters.
 How to Safely Charge Your iPhone 17
 The iPhone 17 is smart about how it handles power, but a few simple habits can help you charge faster, keep the battery healthy, and avoid unnecessary wear over time. Here are key practices to follow:
 Use certified cables and trusted chargers
 Stick with Apple-certified or USB-IF-certified cables and adapters. These meet safety standards and maintain steady power flow, reducing the chance of overheating or voltage spikes.
 If you're using a third-party charger, look for the USB Power Delivery (PD) support and choose reputable brands like Anker . Cheap, uncertified accessories can cause erratic charging or battery strain over time.
 Keep things cool and ventilated
 It's normal for your iPhone to feel a bit warm while charging, especially when it's fast-charging. To keep things safe, charge it in a cool, well-ventilated spot and rest it on a hard, flat surface so heat can escape easily.
 Avoid charging under pillows, blankets, or in direct sunlight, and definitely not inside a hot car. Those conditions trap heat, slow charging, and can wear down the battery over time. If your phone starts to feel hot, just pop off the case for a while and let it breathe.
 Take advantage of built-in battery management
 Avoid repeatedly charging from 0% to 100% if you can. That full cycle stresses the battery more. Partial charging (20-80%) is gentler over time .
 That said, it's fine to leave your iPhone plugged in overnight. Apple's Optimized Battery Charging feature learns your routine and pauses charging at 80% until you need it.
 This helps reduce long-term wear on the lithium-ion cells. You can check or toggle it under Settings → Battery → Charging .
 Keep software updated
 Each iOS update often includes small tweaks to power management and battery health. Staying current helps your iPhone charge more efficiently and safely .
 Conclusion
 Charging your iPhone 17 with an old charger is totally possible. You just need to match the right connector and power standard. Most USB-C adapters from recent iPhones, iPads, or laptops work just fine, while older USB-A bricks will charge more slowly. For the fastest, safest results, go with a quality USB-C PD charger rated 40W or higher, like those from Anker. Whether you reuse what you have or upgrade to a modern fast charger, knowing how your iPhone 17 handles power helps you keep it charged efficiently, and your battery healthy for the long run.

 No, the iPhone 17 doesn't include a charger in the box, just like recent iPhone models. You'll get a 1-meter USB-C to USB-C cable, but you'll need to use your own USB-C Power Delivery (PD) adapter or buy a new one separately. Apple made this change a few years ago to reduce packaging waste and encourage reuse of existing chargers.

 The iPhone 17 series supports up to 40 watts of wired charging through USB Power Delivery (PD). That's higher than previous models like the iPhone 15 and 16, which typically capped around 27 watts. With a 40W or higher USB-C PD charger, you can reach around 50% in 20 minutes.

 To fast charge iPhone 17, you'll need a USB-C PD charger rated at 40W or higher and a USB-C to USB-C cable. Plug in directly, no special settings required. The phone automatically negotiates the fastest safe rate. You'll see the biggest boost up to 80% charge, then the system slows down to protect the battery.
 What kind of charging cable does iPhone 17 use?
 The iPhone 17 has a USB-C port and uses a USB-C to USB-C cable for charging, which is included in the box. To get the fastest charge possible, pair it with a USB-C Power Delivery (PD) adapter rated at 40W or higher, enough to bring the battery to 50% in about 20 minutes.  Ready to buy or unbox an iPhone 17? One question might cross your mind: does iPhone 17 come with charger? Well, if you've owned an iPhone released after 2020, you probably already know the answer: no, it doesn't. Apple stopped including wall chargers a few models ago, and the iPhone 17 continues that trend.
 There are a few fair reasons behind the move. In this guide, you'll learn why Apple made the switch, what's actually in the box, and the best ways to keep your new iPhone 17 powered up every day.
 Table of contents

 FAQs 
 Does the iPhone 17 Come with a Charger?
 The short answer to "Does the new iPhone come with a charger?" is no . Since the iPhone 12 launch back in 2020, Apple has stopped including a power adapter in the box, and the iPhone 17 series is no exception.
 So, what's in the box of the iPhone 17?
 Here's what you'll actually find when you open it:
 The iPhone 17 / 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max handset 
 A USB-C to USB-C charging cable (1 meter) 
 A small pack of paperwork 
 That's it. There's no wall charger , no EarPods , and no SIM ejector tool , since U.S. models now rely entirely on eSIM .
 To charge your new iPhone 17, you'll need a USB-C power adapter to pair with the included USB-C cable. You can use one from a previous device or pick up a new one separately.
 Why does iPhone 17 not come with a charger?
 Now that you know the answer to "Does iPhone come with a charger?" is no , let's talk about why . Here's what's behind Apple's decision:
 Environmental goals. Apple began removing in-box chargers with the iPhone 12 to cut electronic waste and shrink packaging and shipping emissions . Fewer accessories mean less plastic, less metal, and smaller boxes that transport more efficiently.
 You probably already have one. Most users own compatible USB-C power bricks from older devices. Apple encourages people to reuse those rather than add another to the pile.
 A simpler, USB-C ecosystem. With iPhones, iPads, and Macs all using USB-C, you can now rely on one type of charger for everything.
 How Do You Charge the New iPhone 17 Series?
 Even without a charger in the box, powering up your iPhone 17 is easy. You've got three main options: wired USB-C , wireless , and portable chargers for when you're out and about.
 Wired USB-C charger
 The easiest way to charge your iPhone 17 is with the included USB-C cable and a compatible USB-C power adapter .
 This year, the wired charging speed gets a noticeable boost. When paired with a 40W or higher USB-C Power Delivery (PD) adapter, the iPhone 17, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max can reach about 50% in roughly 20 minutes . The ultra-thin iPhone Air still tops out at 20W , similar to earlier entry-level models.
 Apple also introduced a new 40W Dynamic Power Adapter alongside the iPhone 17 series, but it's not required . Any reliable 40W-plus USB-C PD charger will give you the same top speeds. Trusted third-party options from brands like Anker work just as well.
 Using a higher-watt adapter is perfectly safe; your iPhone only pulls the power it needs. If you already have a 20W to 35W PD adapter in good shape, go ahead and reuse it. For everyday charging, it'll still take your phone from empty to about 50% in 25 to 30 minutes , which is enough for many.
 If you're thinking about upgrading your charger, here are some reliable choices from Anker that offer great value:
 Anker Nano Charger (35W) 
 Tired of fishing tangled cables out of your bag? This small Anker Nano Charger (35W) solves that problem. The built-in 2.3-foot retractable USB-C cord tucks neatly inside the body, so it's ready whenever you need it. There's also a second USB-C port , letting you charge two devices at once; the total output is 35W shared between them.
 Inside, Anker's PowerIQ 3.0 tech ensure fast, safe charging for phones, tablets, and earbuds. The retractable cord is tested for about 20,000 pulls , and the charger stays compact enough (like an AirPods case) to toss in a bag or pocket. It's a clean, all-in-one option for everyday use or travel.
 Anker Nano Charger (45W) 
 Want something tiny that still hits full iPhone 17 fast-charge speeds? The Anker Nano Charger (45W) does exactly that. Powered by GaN technology , this single-port adapter is roughly the size of Apple's classic 5W wall brick , only far more capable.
 It outputs up to 45W and supports both USB-C PD and PPS profiles, automatically adjusting power for each device. That means it can take an iPhone 17 Pro Max to 50% in about 20 minutes , deliver Samsung Super Fast Charging 2.0 at full speed for a Galaxy S25 Ultra, and still have enough headroom for tablets or a Nintendo Switch.
 Despite the power, it's easy to carry. The foldable plug keeps it bag-friendly, and Anker's ActiveShield 3.0 monitors temperature millions of times per day to prevent overheating. It's a compact, travel-ready charger that punches well above its size.
 Anker Prime Charger (250W, 6 Ports, GaNPrime) 
 If your desk needs one hub for everything, this Anker Prime Charger (250W) is the do-it-all station. You get 6 USB ports (4× USB-C, 2× USB-A) with up to 250W total output . One of those USB-C ports can deliver 140 watts on its own , enough to power a 16" MacBook Pro at full speed while still charging your phone and tablet.
 A small digital display shows real-time power for each port , and the companion app or the control dial lets you tweak modes like AI Power , Port Priority, or Dual-Laptop easily. It's tidy, fast, and saves you from juggling multiple bricks, perfect for a home office or anyone who runs several devices at once.
 Wireless charger
 If you'd rather skip the cable, you have two solid wireless options: MagSafe and the newer Qi2 standard.
 Not familiar with MagSafe? 
 It's Apple's wireless charging tech, first introduced with the iPhone 12 lineup in 2020. Under the hood, it's still based on the same universal Qi standard used by most smartphones today, but Apple added a ring of magnets around the charging coils inside both the iPhone and charger.
 Those magnets help the charger snap into place every time for precise alignment and more efficient power transfer. 
 How fast is it? Well, first-gen MagSafe chargers, like the Anker 3-in-1 Cube with Qi2 , delivered up to 15W. Apple increased that to 25W with the iPhone 16 series, and this year's iPhone 17 lineup keeps the same 25W cap.
 What about Qi2? 
 It's the open standard that mirrors MagSafe's idea: same magnets, same alignment, similar speeds, but developed by the Wireless Power Consortium . That means more choice from trusted third-party brands, not just Apple's puck.
 The latest Qi2 25W (also called Qi2.2) update is supported right out of the box on the iPhone 17 series . These Qi2.2-certified chargers can reach the same 25W speeds as MagSafe 2.0, filling your battery to about 50% in 30 minutes .
 Already have an older Qi pad? 
 It'll work fine, just slower, around 7.5W on iPhones, and you may need to wiggle the phone slightly to find that "sweet spot."
 Quick wireless charging compatibility guide 
 Wireless charging is still a bit slower than plugging in, but it's clean, simple, and perfect for a nightstand, desk, or car mount.

 True Qi2 25W-certified wireless charging. The magnetic pad delivers the full 25 watts your iPhone 17 can take, keeping alignment perfect every time. The Apple Watch puck is Apple-certified for fast charging, too.
 Aerospace-grade TEC active cooling. A small thermal-electric module holds your phone below 89°F while charging, reducing heat and protecting long-term battery health.
 ActiveShield 5.0 safety. The system runs over 10 million temperature checks per day to maintain safe, steady charging.
 1.65" live display. See real-time power, temperature, and status, or customize it with a screensaver. Instant alerts pop up if anything needs attention.
 Three smart modes. 
 Boost Mode : quick top-ups with gentle cooling.
 Ice Mode : maximum cooling and fastest charge while you're using the phone.
 Sleep Mode : dims the display and silences the fan for overnight charging.
 Smart interaction. Connect via NFC or Bluetooth in the Anker app to check status, schedule modes, or trigger Sleep Mode automatically at night.
 A 65W GaN foldable adapter and a durable USB-C cable are included in the box, so you're ready to go right away.
 Anker Prime Wireless Car Charger 
 This Anker Prime Wireless Car Charger (MagGo, AirCool, Pad) brings full-speed Qi2 25W wireless charging and snap-on alignment to your car and keeps it stable on any road.
 Where it shines: 
 Steady power, even in the heat. The same aerospace-grade TEC cooling tech keeps your phone below 95°F while charging, preventing slowdown or heat-related wear.
 Flexible viewing. Rotate between portrait and landscape, and fine-tune up to ±32° for clear navigation without blocking your view.
 Built to stay put. A strong 13N magnetic hold and locking vent hook keep your phone secure, tested across rough road conditions.
 Tidy setup. Comes with a 60W dual-port car adapter, a USB-C cable, a cord organizer and two cable clips to keep things neat.
 This charger is great for daily drivers who want fast, stable, snap-on wireless charging and a clean dashboard.
 Portable charger
 When you're away from an outlet, a portable charger or power bank keeps your iPhone 17 running.
 Wired power banks with USB-C Power Delivery (PD) at 20W or more are best for fast top-ups.
 MagSafe or Qi2 wireless power banks attach magnetically to the back of your iPhone 17, delivering completely "cable-free" power for travel or a long day out.
 Battery size matters. A 10,000-20,000 mAh capacity usually covers a full day or two without adding too much bulk.
 If you're flying, keep in mind that the FAA allows batteries under 100 Wh without special approval. That's roughly 27,000 mAh at 3.7V per pack.
 Below are two great Anker picks that cover different needs: one pocket-slim, one powerhouse.
 Anker Nano Power Bank (5K) 
 This ultra-slim Anker Nano Power Bank (5K, Slim) is made for everyday carry. The 5,000 mAh capacity gives you just enough juice to top up your iPhone 17 once without weighing down your pocket.
 It snaps magnetically to the back of your phone using Qi2-certified 15W wireless charging , so you can walk, scroll, or take calls while it powers up. There's also a USB-C port that provides up to 20W if you prefer a faster wired charge.
 At just 0.3 inches thick , it slides neatly into a pocket or pouch, while the rounded edges and soft finish feel great in your hand. It's a smart pick for quick top-ups on commutes or nights out when you don't want to carry cables.
 Anker Prime Power Bank (26K, 300W) 
 If you need real power, for your iPhone 17, laptop, or a tablet, this Anker Prime Power Bank (26K, 300W) covers everything. It packs a big 26,250 mAh capacity (right under the FAA's 100 Wh travel limit) and delivers up to 300W total output through two USB-C and one USB-A port.
 Each USB-C port can push up to 140W , enough to fast-charge a 16" MacBook Pro while still powering your phone. A built-in smart display shows how much power each port is drawing. It also supports up to 250W fast recharging , so the bank itself refills quickly between uses.
 Despite the power, it's compact enough for travel and slips easily into a backpack or carry-on.
 Conclusion
 So, does iPhone 17 come with charger? No, and that's now the norm. Apple's move toward eco-conscious packaging means you'll need to reuse your old adapter or buy new. The good news? Charging options have never been more flexible.
 Whether you plug in with a 40W+ USB-C fast charger, go wireless with MagSafe or Qi2, or carry a portable power bank, you've got plenty of ways to stay charged. And at Anker, you'll find smart, fast, and reliable chargers built for the iPhone 17 and beyond.

 How to charge iPhone 17 with old charger?
 If you already have a USB-C power adapter, you can keep using it with the iPhone 17. Just connect the USB-C to USB-C cable included in the box. To get fast charging speeds, you'll need an adapter that supports USB Power Delivery (PD). Older 20W-35W chargers will work fine, but models rated 40W or higher will give you the quickest results, about 50% in roughly 20 minutes.

 Apple keeps the box light and minimal. Inside, you'll find the iPhone 17 handset, a 1-meter USB-C to USB-C cable, and a small pack of paperwork. There's no wall charger, no EarPods, and no SIM tool, since U.S. models now use eSIM only. To charge your iPhone 17, you'll need to pick up a new USB-C adapter separately or use one you already own.

 Go for a USB-C Power Delivery (PD) charger rated at 20W or higher. That's Apple's baseline for fast charging across recent models. For maximum speed, choose a 40W or higher adapter, which can top up the iPhone 17, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max to about 50% in 20 minutes.  With a 40W or higher USB-C Power Delivery (PD) charger, the iPhone 17 series can reach around 50% in 20 minutes and a full charge in roughly 1 hour and 20 minutes. Wireless charging is a bit slower. You may need a Dynamic Power Adapter from Apple

According to the official specs of the iPhone 17, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max, they can charge to 50% in just 20 minutes, while the iPhone Air gets to 50% in 30 minutes. However, that charging speed is achieved with Apple’s new “40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max”, which is quite special for two reasons.


First, the horrible name is actually Apple being brutally honest about the charger’s abilities. While it can reach 60W, that’s only for a limited time before it gets too hot and slows down to 40W. According to a test by Reddit user privatebok over at the r/UsbCHardware subreddit, that time is about 18 minutes.

Second, it supports the new Adjustable Voltage Supply (AVS) protocol, which uses granular voltage options for more precise and efficient charging. That way, the charger chooses a specific voltage for the fastest possible charging, without overheating the battery.

What’s unclear about the new iPhone models is whether they will require an AVS charger for fast charging. Most chargers you have are likely to support only the older Programmable Power Supply (PPS) protocol, which can handle 40W, 60W, or even higher, but doesn’t provide the granular voltage options of AVS.


It’s more than a bad name, though


The standards supported by Apple's new charger. | Image by privaterbok on Reddit




Another annoying issue with Apple’s new charger is that it doesn’t support PPS at all. Instead, it only has the standard USB Power Delivery 3.0, which means it might not be very useful for charging other devices. That’s a bummer for a $39 product.

Google, on the other hand, has its own Pixel Flex Dual Port 67W USB-C Fast Charger, which supports AVS, but also USB PD 3.2 and PPS. That one also has two USB-C ports and reaches 67W, so it might fast charge more devices. It is a bit more expensive, though, and it costs $59.99.


That’s the Apple way

Apple is one of the few companies that adopt new standards and stick to them, though in its own way. USB-C got faster adoption thanks to being the only port on any new MacBook, way before it became the standard port on most devices. Well, Apple was also the last smartphone manufacturer to switch to USB-C, so it’s not all pretty.


So, using a new charging standard may feel painful at first, but I believe it is the right decision. The only issue is that the rest of the industry usually follows slowly.

 You'll also need a compatible charger to get the top speeds 
 Only one matching charger is currently available, from Apple 
 The Apple iPhone 17 series is now official, but we're still learning some of the finer details of these phones and their specs: and it seems that you're going to need a specific charger to get the fastest charging speeds from the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max.
 As discovered by tipster ShrimpApplePro (via 9to5Mac ), the impressive charging times of these two premium handsets – up to 50% of a charge in as little as 20 minutes – are down to support for the USB-PD (Power Delivery) system.
 In particular, it uses the USB-PD 3.2 SPR AVS specification, and at the moment the only charger on the market that supports the same standard is Apple's own 40W Dynamic Power Adaptor, launched alongside the iPhone 17 phones and priced at $39 (about £30 / AU$60). What's more, Apple only sells it in certain regions, and it's not available in the EU or in Australia at the time of writing.
